column2: Act Five
Dandelion
Dandelion

He pushed open the door and looked up at the rain pouring from the sky. Pulling his collar over his head, he grabbed his suitcase and ran. The Panamera's door swung open and he dove into the passenger seat before looking back. Across the curtain of rain, on the other side of the floor-to-ceiling windows, the air-conditioning scattered the last tiny parachutes. Chen Wenwen stood amid the drifting dandelion seeds, as though she might float away with those soft white things. Looking toward him, she breathed a small patch of mist onto the glass and drew a smiling face in three strokes.
“Mingfei, is it hard, being abroad all by yourself?” Chen Wenwen asked softly, looking down at her plate rather than at him.
“It's all right, really. I have a senior roommate named Fingel, and a boss named Caesar. They're both great to me.” Lu Mingfei's voice echoed through every corner of Aspasia.

Before the revolution the building had been a French merchant's house. Aspasia had renovated it after buying it, preserving the old elm floors but knocking out all four walls and replacing them with floor-to-ceiling windows. The rooms had been opened into one another and the upper floors removed, leaving an eight-meter-high vaulted ceiling. An enormous chandelier hung from wooden beams nearly a century old. The chandelier was dark now; the only light in the vast space came from the candles on Lu Mingfei and Chen Wenwen's table. Theirs was the only occupied table, too.
Boss Caesar—or rather, the Mint Club—had made a flamboyant gesture and booked the whole place!
Chen Wenwen wore the white dress Lu Mingfei knew so well, white lace-trimmed socks, and flat black leather shoes. Candlelight brushed her with a faint warmth.

Lu Mingfei wore formal black, with a Florentine-style shirt and mother-of-pearl buttons. The outfit had been waiting in the BMW's back seat, thoughtfully arranged by the Mint Club in keeping with Mr. Caesar Gattuso's usual standards of dress.
To their left stood an enormous antique ship, planted upright with its bow nearly touching the roof. It was a Ming dynasty wreck that Aspasia had salvaged and ingeniously turned into a wine cabinet.
On the right was a huge window, with a tree-lined road beyond it and a river beyond the road. Rain rattled against the glass.

Lu Mingfei had never eaten a meal so formally in his life. He sat bolt upright as though someone had shoved a rolling pin down his back, elbows raised, fork in his left hand and knife in his right, cutting his lamb chops with painstaking precision. He was afraid he'd have to pay for the clothes if he wrinkled them. There had been no ordering: their likes and dietary restrictions were already on file. The waiter said that after receiving the request, the executive chef had personally selected the finest ingredients. The cheese had aged five years in an Italian cave, the chops were guaranteed to come from six-month-old Italian goats, and the fish had arrived fresh from Yokohama. Every dish was impressive. Lu Mingfei couldn't understand the strange names, but he got the idea.

Each course came with a different wine. Lu Mingfei had little interest in the sour, astringent stuff, but this was no time to embarrass himself; he wasn't eating with Fingel! Every bite and sip... was it food? No, it was sophistication! He ate with an air of refinement, feeling tremendously cool.
“At first I thought you were joking.” Chen Wenwen took a sip of wine. “I looked up this restaurant online. They're applying for three Michelin stars, and the prices are frightening.”
Lu Mingfei nodded with a flourish. “Authentic Italian food, a bit of a niche taste. It's normal for it to cost more.”

His knowledge of Italian food actually began and ended with pizza. But with a boy and girl facing each other by flickering candlelight, whispering together, who would mention pizza? Wasn't it basically a meat-stuffed flatbread? He had to talk about respectable things like foie gras, white truffles, lobster, and Black Sea caviar.
“The wine is wonderful,” Chen Wenwen said. “Mingfei, did you learn to drink red wine in America?”
“Oh... some are fuller-bodied, and some have a stronger fruit flavor. Drink enough and you learn to tell.” Lu Mingfei licked his lips. They were drinking a 1997 Margaux.

Everything he knew about wine came from Fingel, who occasionally ordered a bottle of red to whet his appetite during late-night meals. But Fingel always chose table wine as sour as aged vinegar, with a standing in its French region much like cheap bulk liquor sold by weight at a rural Chinese supply cooperative. Lafite, Latour, Margaux, the great Bordeaux estates—Fingel never even looked at them. He couldn't afford them.
“I've never seen you in a suit. It fits you rather well.” Chen Wenwen glanced at him.

Lu Mingfei's back stiffened a little more of its own accord. He had worn a Korean-style suit to the Literature Club's graduation party, playing the lowercase i for Zhao Menghua, but Chen Wenwen had forgotten. Of course, that suit couldn't compare with this one. This was Caesar's standard. Nono said Caesar was outrageously picky about clothes: he never wore anything ready-made, always ordering from a little tailor that kept paper patterns of his measurements for every age from five to eighteen. A phone call was enough to order a suit. It was practically the Gattuso family's own imperial workshop.
“If I'd known it was this sort of occasion, I'd have dressed more formally,” Chen Wenwen added.
“You look great like that.” Gathering his courage, Lu Mingfei surveyed her from the tips of her hair to her toes, delighted.

How could she not? In his memory, Chen Wenwen always wore this dress, so white it was almost translucent, sitting on a bench in the sun with a book. Without it she hardly seemed like Chen Wenwen at all.

Throughout high school, even when he managed to get very close to her, he had still felt as if he were watching from a distance. Boys of every kind had always surrounded her, all more accomplished than Lu Mingfei, making him ashamed to squeeze in. Now she wore the same white dress, a warm glow flowing over her skin, only fifty—perhaps forty—centimeters away. He could lift his eyes to meet her gentle gaze and smell the soft fragrance of her hair. He could study her freely, without restraint, like dissecting a little frog in biology class when the teacher made them examine it millimeter by millimeter... And where were all those boys who used to surround Chen Wenwen? Ha! Not one could come between them. Tonight, at Aspasia... he'd booked the whole place!
Music drifted almost imperceptibly through the room. Lu Mingfei could barely contain himself.
“This song is nice.” He began putting on airs as an art connoisseur.
“It's Dalida's ‘I Found My Love in Portofino.’ You like it too?” Chen Wenwen's eyes lit up with delighted surprise. “Lu Mingfei... you've changed.”

He blinked and couldn't help looking down at his reflection in a sterling-silver spoon. Had he changed? Become suave? Was he no longer that shabby little loser? Could he now eat Italian food and appreciate Dalida too?
At last the great day had come: the turtle had turned over!

He had always hated the rich kids in class, showing off their family vacations abroad, their new houses, casually displaying the logos on their designer clothes, climbing into their family's fine cars on rainy days and waving goodbye to classmates miserably waiting under the eaves for the rain to stop... How vulgar! Yet the girls had no restraint; those young masters' airs always left them dazzled, eyes sparkling. But now that it was his turn to show off, he suddenly found it wonderfully comfortable, enough to make him float with bliss!
Lu Mingfei leaned over the table, bringing his face a little closer to Chen Wenwen's, so restless with excitement he was almost ready to take flight.
Chu Zihang reached out with a trembling hand and switched off the Panamera's engine. The headlights went out, leaving the garage in darkness.

He breathed deeply and silently, gathering strength. Only when he felt able to move again did he turn on the overhead reading light, remove his sunglasses, and put his black contacts back in. He got out, stripped off his FedEx uniform, and changed into tennis clothes, rubbing a little dust onto his chest. His head was covered in cold sweat, his hair soaked; that needed no disguise. In the mirror he did look as though he had come back exhausted from the tennis court.

As he crossed the lawn, concealed sprinklers rose from the ground and rotated, spraying him. The cold water made him feel weak; his vision blurred in waves. He had little strength left, perhaps enough to walk a few hundred meters, and had to use it carefully. It would be best if neither parent were home, so no one would stop him in the living room for a conversation.

Chu Zihang pushed the door open cautiously and paused. His mother was curled up asleep on the sofa. At this hour she was usually out at a bar, laughing and talking loudly over whiskey or brandy with her friends. For some reason tonight was an exception.

She slept terribly. Once asleep, the woman was utterly careless. Who knew how many times she'd rolled around? Besides boldly exposing an entire thigh, she'd wrinkled her silk nightdress until it looked like a rag. She held a thin blanket to her chest like a child sleeping with a doll. The air conditioner was still set to the temperature Chu Zihang had chosen before leaving, but that had been a sunlit morning, and now a storm had broken on the evening. He didn't know what expression to give a mother like this. Passing the sofa, he smelled a strong odor of alcohol. He tugged the blanket over her and went upstairs straight to the bathroom.

He bolted the door and checked the lock to make sure no one would burst in. Leaning against it, he breathed in short, silent gasps, pressing one hand to his waist while pulling off his tennis shirt with the other. It was soaked with cold sweat. In the mere few dozen meters from the garage, the wound beneath the layers of tissue pressed to his lower right abdomen had begun to scab, only to split open again when he moved. A thin stream of blood ran down his body. He took the medicine box from a wall cabinet and found tetanus vaccine, iodine, and bandages.

He peeled away the blood-soaked tissues to reveal a crudely dressed wound. The dressing was so rough it was alarming. Chu Zihang had used clear packing tape—the kind used to seal cardboard boxes, complete with a company logo printed on it. It was all he could find at the time, so he had sealed himself up like a broken carton, as long as the blood didn't leak out where the Maintenance Department could see.
Gritting his teeth, Chu Zihang tore off the tape. Blood welled out. He blotted it with toilet paper and felt something inside the wound.

A sharp shard of glass, roughly an inch long, buried all the way in. When the suspended platform fell, his abdomen had struck the shattered glass curtain wall. Because he had undergone blood amplification in time, his dragon bloodline had made his body exceptionally resilient, and the rush of adrenaline had kept him from feeling pain. But when the effect wore off, the pain returned with vengeful force. His body was still human, after all.

Even through the tissue, touching the glass made him convulse. It seemed to have grown into his body, become one of his bones; pulling it out was like tearing out a bone of his own. He bit down on a rolled towel, took several deep breaths, and pulled hard... Tiny drops of blood spattered half the mirror.

The instant of agony nearly drained his strength, and darkness filled his vision. Half a minute passed before he could see again. He looked at the bloody shard and laid it gently on the edge of the sink.

After blotting the blood, he inserted a disposable syringe into the deltoid of his upper arm and injected the tetanus vaccine. Then he wiped the wound directly with an alcohol-soaked cotton ball. It was like cutting the wound open again, but there was no better disinfectant in the household kit. By the time all the cotton balls were red, the bleeding had stopped. He spread Yunnan Baiyao ointment on a piece of gauze, pressed it to the wound, and wound a bandage around his waist. He changed into a white shirt and tucked it into his jeans, concealing the bandage completely.
He studied himself in the mirror. Nothing looked unusual except that his face was a little paler.

He put all the bloody cotton, tissues, syringe, and glass into his tennis bag, wiped the blood from the floor, and checked every corner of the bathroom to be sure he had left no trace. He would never leave a trace. The Chu Zihang who lived in this house was someone else, unconnected to Cassell College: a good student, obedient, fond of basketball and books, with no bad habits or violent tendencies, whose favorite celebrity was even a wholesome role model, Wang Leehom. Sometimes Chu Zihang himself thought such a person was as pale and lifeless as a paper figure, but his parents were proud of their paper-perfect son.
If they saw these bloodstained things, they probably wouldn't be proud. They would think they had raised a monster.
No one liked monsters, and Chu Zihang didn't blame them, so he put on that pale, pleasing face. He wanted his parents to be happy; whether the person they saw was real didn't matter.
A packed suitcase and a laptop bag were always waiting in his bedroom, ready for departure at any time. Chu Zihang checked that his passport was valid, picked up his luggage, and went downstairs.
His mother was still asleep on the sofa, clutching the blanket tightly.

Chu Zihang took a cushion, tugged the blanket free, and slipped the cushion into her arms. She held it and slept on, breathing softly through her nose. He tucked the blanket around her on all four sides and sat watching her face. Apparently she hadn't gone out today and hadn't put on makeup. Without it she looked a little older, with fine lines at the corners of her eyes. A woman who had been too beautiful in her youth, showing her age after drinking, made a desolate sight.

It was hard to accept that such a woman was his mother. The most reliable thing he remembered her doing for him was giving birth to him. According to that man, she'd wanted to give up even then, saying childbirth would hurt and perhaps she should have an abortion. Unfortunately for her, she was eight months pregnant when she changed her mind, and the doctor warned her that an abortion then would be suicide. Thus Chu Zihang had survived. From the time he could understand speech, the woman had held him and said, Mommy suffered so much giving birth to you, so grow up quickly and take care of Mommy; Mommy works so hard, so grow up quickly and earn money to support Mommy; there are so many bad people in the world, so grow up quickly and protect Mommy... Mommy was so fragile, so tired, had suffered so much... Because Mommy had such a hard time, she missed parents' meetings, nobody packed his lunch for school outings, nobody picked him up in the rain. When he had a high fever... Mommy did stay with him, but she had no idea how to care for a feverish child, so she gave him neither medicine nor water. Instead she touched his little forehead and said, “Are you dizzy? Mommy will sing Zihang a lovely song!”
No one had ever promised to protect Chu Zihang, yet from childhood he had felt he must take care of many people.

Rain whispered against the windows. His mother turned over and kicked at him unconsciously; he tucked the blanket around her again. He probably wouldn't have a chance to say goodbye before leaving. That was his mother, careless and oblivious: once asleep, she slept like the dead, and waking her would only make her angry.
Aunt Tong, the housekeeper, came in, wiping her hands on her apron. “Zihang, are you going out?” She had seen his suitcase.
“Yes. The school moved up the start of the short term and told us to report back.” He nodded. “I'm taking a night flight.”
“Oh! Why didn't you tell your parents? The whole family could have dinner together and have the driver take you.”
“I told them yesterday. ‘Dad’ has a business dinner tonight.”
“Your ‘dad’ is dining with people from the land bureau tonight,” Aunt Tong said. She meant that he had important clients to see and couldn't help missing the chance to see him off.
“It's fine,” Chu Zihang said.

He had no doubt that if “Dad” had time, he would arrange to take him out to dinner. Dad was so successful in business because he handled every social obligation well. He handled Chu Zihang well too, never missing a gift or a courtesy, leaving no fault to find. But Chu Zihang didn't need to be treated as an obligation, so he had deliberately announced his departure only the day before, when “Dad's” dinner with the land bureau could no longer be rescheduled.
“Don't let Mom sleep in the living room again. She'll catch cold,” he said.
“No, no, she only just fell asleep,” Aunt Tong said quickly. “She was in the kitchen cooking something and sent me to the supermarket for vinegar. When I got back, she was asleep.”
“Cooking?” Chu Zihang stared. How strange. The saying “she wouldn't even right an overturned oil bottle” might have been invented for his mother.
“Oh no! She doesn't know how to use the stove. Something might happen in the kitchen!”

They hurried in and were hit by a burnt smell. Smoke filled the kitchen; the range hood wasn't even on. A little more and the smoke alarm would have sounded. Chu Zihang shut off the gas and opened every window. Once some smoke had cleared, Aunt Tong took a blackened pot off the stove. It was imported German stainless steel, polished daily until it could serve as a mirror.
“What is that?” Chu Zihang covered his nose. Everything in the pot had burned to charcoal; he couldn't tell what it had been.

He guessed Aunt Annie had taken his mother to another fashionable cooking class and inspired her to try her hand. Those classes were fun: a group of ladies carrying LV, Chanel, and Gucci bags were taught by a chef who played the master, making dishes like king crab with coconut and egg white paired with the Trimbach family's Alsatian Pinot Gris, or pork and green plums with tiger-paw mushrooms paired with a royal dry red from the Gigondas estate. His mother would come home and practice on Chu Zihang. Each time he faced an indistinct heap on a bone-china plate, he would try a little and suggest, “Mom, would you like to taste it too?” She would taste it and pull a long face. “What I made in class was clearly nothing like this!” Chu Zihang understood why. In class the ingredients were prepared for her and a chef stood behind her giving instructions in real time. Cook that way, and even an old man selling Shaanxi meat sandwiches could make authentic French food.
“It won't come clean. Throw the pot away too,” he said.
“I understand! Your mother was boiling dumplings!” Aunt Tong slapped her thigh.
Chu Zihang blinked. Dumplings? Did she mean Italian pasta? “Matsutake pasta in broth with Riesling”? That had failed last time, and afterward his mother had sworn never to make it again.
“Dumplings before a journey, noodles on return. Your mother was making dumplings for you,” Aunt Tong said. “She's from Shaanxi.”

Chu Zihang touched his chest without thinking. Something deep inside twitched faintly. Flour lay scattered across the stainless-steel kitchen island, with a thick rolling pin lying across it... No wonder his mother had sent Aunt Tong to buy vinegar: it was for dumplings. Dumplings before departure, noodles on return; before a journey, you always ate a bowl of dumplings. No fashionable cooking-class chef would have taught her this. She could only have learned it from Grandma: handmade celery-and-pork dumplings paired with a selected 2010 Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar.
No wonder she hadn't gone out. He had thought it was because of the rain.
He fished a piece of wrapper out of the pot and put it in his mouth. The flavor was truly something. His nostrils filled with burnt smoke, as though someone had used him for a chimney.
“It's inedible. Better throw it out,” he said, swallowing it anyway.

Washing his hands at the sink, he thought of that man again. His life had always seemed absurd: a complete loser, boasting about irrelevant things, smiling apologetically as he drove people around, watching his wife take their son and leave. Only at the end had he revealed his terrifying bloodline. With that man's blood, so much should have been within easy reach.
A dragon bloodline that stood above ordinary people and could kill as easily as cutting down straw dogs.
If he was that powerful, why hide his blood, humble himself to serve his wife and make her happy, and live a “normal” life?

What was a hybrid? A different kind of being, between human and dragon. Even if what you did concerned humanity's survival, you were not truly human yourself; when your blood burned, your pupils turned gold like a dragon's. Through golden dragon eyes the world looked entirely different. Dragons killed and judged decisively, strength determining rank. If their world had a ranking system like Blizzard's ladder, blood and death would constantly wash the board clean.
A king was always killed by a new king.
And yet did he still want somewhere to return to, even a doghouse? Did he want... a home?

“Aunt Tong, remember to remind Mom to drink milk every day.” Chu Zihang opened the refrigerator and showed her a carton. “Buy this Sanyuan low-fat milk. She won't drink any other kind. Add a sugar cube, microwave it on low for five minutes, and make sure she drinks it before bed every night.”
“I know, I know, same as always.” Aunt Tong didn't quite understand this habit. Before every trip abroad he repeated the whole procedure as though entrusting her with some momentous responsibility.
“I'll leave the car in the airport parking lot, with the key and parking card in the glove compartment. Have the driver take the spare key and bring it back.” Chu Zihang said. “I'm going.”
“Zihang, aren't you going to say goodbye to your mother?”
“I'm not used to saying goodbye... Whenever she sees me off... she kisses me like crazy...” He picked up his suitcase and disappeared into the rain.
“Sir, would you like to come over and select a dessert wine?” The sommelier materialized behind Lu Mingfei like a ghost.
Lu Mingfei thought, Honestly... why appear like a ghost now and poke your nose in? But perhaps it was an Italian dining custom. He nodded politely to Chen Wenwen. “I'll be right back.”

The sommelier led him into the shadow of the antique ship wine cabinet, pointing out little golden bottles of dessert wine while lowering his voice. “Booking the whole restaurant is quite a gesture. Is this a special occasion? Would you like to surprise the lady when dessert is served?”
“A surprise? Extra whipped cream?” Lu Mingfei didn't understand.
“Have you seen Spider-Man 2?” the sommelier patiently explained. “Spider-Man proposes to his girlfriend over dinner and has the waiter put the diamond ring in her champagne...”
“Soga!” Enlightenment struck Lu Mingfei like a revelation.

A sophisticated, romantic setting like this, a rainy night separating two people from the world, a fine Italian meal and a little wine, Dalida singing softly in the air, candlelight spilling over the girl's white dress—shouldn't he be itching to... no, shouldn't he let his feelings move him to say something important? This was a stage made for a confession! The girl was watching him, eyes lowered, cheeks flushed. The spotlight was already on him, the microphone in his hand, the audience waiting to cheer. If he didn't say something earth-shaking, it would be a crime against heaven!
“I don't have a ring... And we're not at the proposal stage yet, are we?” He scratched his head.

“No problem, we're here to help! For example, we could decorate the cheesecake with the most important words from the time you met and came to know each other.” The sommelier gave an emphatic thumbs-up. “Our service is first-rate!”
“Oh! That's a real bargain!” Lu Mingfei beamed, rubbing his hands, eager to try.
“Then what were the words that laid the foundation of your relationship?”
Lu Mingfei looked up at the ceiling. Candlelight illuminated his eyes, faint flames stirring in them, his face blooming with romance.
Pen and paper in hand, the sommelier held his breath and waited.
“There weren't any,” Lu Mingfei sighed.
The sommelier pressed a hand to his forehead. Was this distinguished guest inarticulate, or simply too shy?
“Then put the Olympic rings on it!” Lu Mingfei suddenly said.
“Oh, yes.” The sommelier nodded blankly.

Lu Mingfei returned to the table. Chen Wenwen was playing with the floating candle; she gave him a sweet smile and said little. He smiled back, finishing the last pieces of lamb while waiting for his Olympic cheesecake. What could the sommelier know about the twists of his thoughts? He was remembering the high-school sports meet in his second year. His event had been the five-thousand-meter run. Nobody had forced him to sign up. Chen Wenwen was running it too, and since boys and girls ran together and he fancied his endurance, he could show off in front of her. But who could have guessed? Chen Wenwen looked delicate, yet she had been on the track team in elementary school. At the starting gun she had shot away, running right behind Xu Yanyan and using him to block the wind. On the final lap she made her move and took second place among the girls. Lu Mingfei, meanwhile, was still a whole lap behind, shuffling along with groans. He had been knocked down at the start, scraped his knee on the track, and fallen into last place. The five thousand meters was the final event; only he remained on the track, and everyone else had slipped away after watching the race. Just as he was wondering whether to change direction and run straight for the exit, Chen Wenwen crossed the field and ran beside him. “Come on, come on! Nobody in our Literature Club can be left behind!” she had said. She'd worn a white T-shirt with the Olympic rings on her chest, so lovely he wanted to lean against her or something.
What a memorable event! He could count it as the beginning of their romance!

He slipped into a mood of predestined love, convinced that he and Chen Wenwen, not Zhao Menghua, had been exchanging meaningful glances all along. Every great lover had that potential: see a pretty girl and imagine fate had already bound you together, like Jia Baoyu's famous “I've seen this girl before.” In short, he was lovestruck.
“Lu Mingfei, didn't that senior who picked you up last time come back with you?” Chen Wenwen asked suddenly.

It was like a bucket of cold water over his head. His lovestruck haze faded, and an image of the little red-haired witch rose in his mind, her silver four-leaf-clover earrings swinging beside her ears.
“She's probably on vacation with her boyfriend,” he said quietly.
The little witch's image kept bouncing like a spring-loaded puppet. Oh, stop bouncing. This isn't your scene to be the heroine; Caesar is your leading man... Lu Mingfei's thoughts were a mess.

Could a person like two girls at once? He'd read a psychology article saying no: a man like Duan Zhengchun could not exist. If someone claimed to like two girls at the same time, he liked neither. So between Nono and Chen Wenwen he could only like one; the other was merely adolescent male hormones stirring. Which one, which one?
Lu Mingfei was nineteen and had been single all nineteen years. He wanted very much to like a girl seriously.

Yes, yes, Nono was wonderful. She drove a flaming-red Ferrari and wore a flaming-red bikini. Her rare A-rank bloodline made her exceptional even among hybrids. She was only twenty, but in high heels she could command a room like a little queen, drawing every eye. At twenty-five, who knew how magnificent she'd be? And her mind twisted and turned, a book you could never finish or fully understand but always wanted to read. If you were with her, you'd have something to do for the rest of your life: study her. You wouldn't have to worry about making a living in later years either. The little witch seemed to come from a distinguished family and was very dependable.

In short, everything about Nono was wonderful; beside her, Chen Wenwen was only an ordinary girl. But Nono was too far away. He was her little sidekick, always at her beck and call, and only Caesar was worthy of her.
Would you choose a goddess at the edge of the sky, or the girl right in front of you?
Chen Wenwen is looking at you! She's probably waiting for you to say something!

Stop thinking, brother! There's no future following the little witch! At best it's a toad's rhapsody about coveting a swan! How did the old saying go? A bird in the hand is worth ten in the bush! A little crow on the branch beats a golden phoenix in the sky! Think about it: say the words now and you might finally leave the ranks of the single! You'd have a girlfriend! You've never even put your arm around a girl's waist in your life! Never had a Valentine's chocolate of your own! Don't you want something this wonderful? Just say the words! Only a word from you! A natural eight-hearts-and-eight-arrows diamond necklace can be yours for 998 yuan! Limited quantities, hurry! Pick up the phone and order...

Something strange seemed to have crept into his thoughts... Back on track... Don't you want something this wonderful? Just say the words! You'd never again have to spend Valentine's Day watching Brokeback Mountain with Fingel! You might even get a first kiss as a bonus! Look at Chen Wenwen's lips, soft as petals in the candlelight, and dare say you aren't tempted!
Ten million little devils danced in Lu Mingfei's heart.

Damn it! It was settled! Youth was wasted if you didn't chase girls! What the hell was he waiting for? Wait any longer and the daylilies would go cold! Forget the decorated cheesecake. A confession needed only a mouth!
He jerked his head up and looked across the table. “I actually like...”
“Calm down. Don't spit food in my face.” Across the table, Lu Mingze calmly cut a slice of tuna belly.

Not Lu Mingfei's plump, round cousin, but the devilish Lu Mingze who had bargained for his life. The little fellow's hair was meticulously combed. His formal black suit, stand-collar shirt, bow tie, and lace-edged handkerchief in his breast pocket matched the establishment perfectly, as though he belonged here for dinner and Chen Wenwen in her plain white dress was the one out of place.
Speak of the devil and the devil appears!
“I wasn't going to spit in your face,” Lu Mingfei began, then suddenly raised his plate. “I was going to smash this over your head!”
“You struggled with yourself so long I got bored waiting, so I summoned you for a chat. Oh, and happy birthday, Brother.” Lu Mingze raised his glass, took a sip, and suddenly frowned.

“Of the five great Bordeaux estates, Margaux is my least favorite. It's a Bordeaux vineyard, but its wine tastes a little like Burgundy.” He sniffed the wine and shook his head. “The tuna belly is perfectly seared, though if I'd made it I'd season it with matsutake rather than truffle. Let me taste your lamb...”
Lu Mingfei shoved him away with a palm to the forehead and swallowed the remaining lamb in a few bites.
“So stingy. I only wanted a piece of lamb,” Lu Mingze said.
“Just letting you have something go wrong for once, so you won't always be leading me around by the nose,” Lu Mingfei grumbled.

“How could that be? You're my most important customer. Until you've used your three remaining summons, I'll serve you faithfully.” Lu Mingze smiled. “But don't worry, we never force a sale. You didn't summon me this time. This is a voluntary customer follow-up.”
“If there's nothing else, disappear! I'm having dinner with my first...” Lu Mingfei stopped. Chen Wenwen wasn't his “first girlfriend.”
“The first girl you secretly loved,” Lu Mingze supplied the correct definition.
“Get lost! Anyway, I'm eating with a beautiful girl. Could you please send me back to the real world? How can I have an appetite looking at you?”

“I like the atmosphere here.” Ignoring him, Lu Mingze looked around. “The old ship harmonizes with the aged elm floor, but the designer has divided the space in a very modern way with marble and resin panels. Old and new fit together beautifully; it's private yet open. No wonder they charge so much.”
“What are you going on about? What's it to you? If there's nothing else, please get lost.”

“I especially like this table. It seems ordinary, but anyone sitting here can see in every direction, as though commanding the whole space.” Lu Mingze pushed aside his plate and glass, rested his elbows on the table, and folded his hands under his chin, looking into Lu Mingfei's eyes. “This is a position of power and authority.”
“Here we go again...” Lu Mingfei covered his face.
“You don't like it? But you've already felt the pleasure power brings, haven't you?” Lu Mingze smiled.
“What pleasure of power? It's the pleasure of chasing a girl. Has your brain overheated?”

“You've never felt this kind of control before, have you? That certainty of victory, holding something firmly in your hand without fear it will escape.” Lu Mingze lifted his glass. “A bottle of the finest red wine and an ordinary one are made much the same way: grapes are grown, fermented in oak barrels, filtered, bottled, and sold. Yet the first costs thousands of times more. Many people can't tell the difference in taste without drinking them side by side, but still claim to love the art of wine and eagerly collect the most expensive bottles. Do you know why?”
“To show off their money.”

“No, not just that. Tasting the most expensive wine makes them feel they possess power. So much invisible value attaches to an expensive bottle: the winemaker's care, the taster's praise, the fashionable crowd's acclaim. The bottle costs eight thousand yuan not because the wine itself is worth that, but because of those invisible values spreading out like a spiderweb. They are worth far more than the wine.” Lu Mingze spoke softly. “When humans taste it, it's like sipping the essence of power, bright red, the color of blood.”
“Could you please break the habit of never saying anything plainly?” Lu Mingfei was sick of the boy's mystical tone.
“You were happy just now. I could feel it,” Lu Mingze said.
“All right, you're the roundworm in my belly. No objection. Next time I'll strain hard and pull you out...” Lu Mingfei said fiercely.

“You were happy because you used to look up to Chen Wenwen. If you were on classroom duty together and she smiled at you, it became a precious memory. But now it's different. You're in the seat of honor at Aspasia, drinking wine that costs eight thousand a bottle, eating food the executive chef spent the afternoon preparing. A luxury car is outside waiting to take you to the airport, and the waiter in the corner awaits your slightest signal, a snap of the fingers, for instance!” Lu Mingze held up a hand and snapped crisply. “A hot Earl Grey, please.”
The waiter came silently to the table and poured amber tea into a glass, apparently unaware that the guest had changed.
Without looking at him, Lu Mingze waved him away coldly. The waiter bowed and vanished into the unlit darkness.

“That is power. It's the smallest kind, yet it still has power's intoxicating scent.” Lu Mingze smelled his fingertips and glanced at Lu Mingfei. “You've caught the scent already, haven't you? Right now Chen Wenwen is prey within your grasp. You have power and no longer need to look up to her. Instead you compare her with Nono. There's nothing she does better than Nono; she's just an ordinary girl. But Nono is too far away, beyond your reach. The power you hold isn't enough, so you still have to look up to Nono, but not to Chen Wenwen. You could even bend down...” He paused. A tissue rose from the table without a breeze and drifted to the floor.
Lu Mingze bent slowly, picked it up, and tossed it before Lu Mingfei. “Pick her up. Forgive her for everything she's done to you.”
Lu Mingfei looked at the tissue. His heart clenched. Blood soaked it, a vivid red heart so bright it seemed ready to drip onto the table.
“Do you... still want her?” Lu Mingze asked softly.
“Take that damn thing away!” Lu Mingfei burst out.
“It's ketchup... I got it on there by accident.” Lu Mingze shrugged. “A joke... just a joke.”
“Damn it!” Lu Mingfei touched his chest, breathing hard.

“Without power, anyone feels inferior, like a stag without antlers that has no place in the herd.” Lu Mingze played with the sterling-silver knife, watching its light turn in his hand. “But for someone who holds power, the girl once beyond his reach becomes a clay doll in the dust, and the enemy who towered above him kneels and begs for mercy. That's power and authority. You can call it the devil, but everyone rejoices to obtain it. Once they've tasted it, they fall in love and long to hold more and more. Have you imagined that one day, just as you face Chen Wenwen today, you might consider bending down to pick up Nono? To the you of that day, she too would be only a clay doll in the dust. She could no longer tease you, no longer wear that proud expression. Even if she cried and begged, you wouldn't be moved. That kind of power... is within your reach, if you only want it.”

Lu Mingfei shuddered violently, unable to control it, as if a cold snake had slithered across his chest. Though Lu Mingze was certainly mischievous, most of the time Lu Mingfei regarded him as being on his side, and deep down half doubted the contract that traded away his life. But as Lu Mingze spoke, uncanny golden light danced in his deep pupils, and a sneering demon hid beneath his mild tone.
Mocking the whole world, every person in it.

Could that day really come? Even if Nono cried and begged him, he wouldn't be moved? Impossible, right? With the little witch's stubborn nature, if she cried, the sun would rise in the west, the Happy Prince would damn well break his heart, and monks would return to worldly life. Could his own steadfast heart remain unmoved? Ridiculous! Even if he practiced some secret art of perfect detachment, could he become that cold? No, no, impossible, absolutely impossible!
“Pah, pah!” Lu Mingfei spat twice into his palm and held it out. “Come on! I've spat in my hand. Give me that power.”
Lu Mingze paused, then smiled. “I can. You just have to beg me.”
“Please, little brother, give me power. I really want to see what Nono looks like begging me.” Lu Mingfei shamelessly put on a pleading face.
At last Lu Mingze was at a loss. He shook his head with a rueful smile. “Brother, you aren't truly begging.”
“If you can't do it, why talk so big? Acting all impressive, having fun pretending to be grown-up?” Lu Mingfei rallied at once. “Pfft!”
He didn't want to take Lu Mingze seriously. The more seriously he considered the boy's words, the more frightening they became; only by dismissing him as a little brat could he feel at ease.

“But one day you will sincerely beg me, and then I will give you everything I promised... I'll go now. Brother, you're nineteen; please patronize my business as often as possible. A pleasure working with you.” Lu Mingze hopped down from the chair. He was the size of an eight- or nine-year-old; seated, his feet couldn't even reach the floor.
“Hey, let me ask you. Who do you think is better... Chen Wenwen or Nono?” Lu Mingfei caught his arm.
“Nono,” Lu Mingze said without thinking.
“Why?”
“I prefer a good figure to the literary type.” Lu Mingze looked utterly serious.
Everything went black before Lu Mingfei's eyes.
“Oh, crap!” His heart went cold.

In the instant of darkness, the person opposite had turned back into Chen Wenwen. His mouth was wide open, looking as though he were about to lean in for a French kiss. She showed no intention of dodging, watching his eyes intently.
Damn it, what power did that little devil use? Jotaro Kujo's Star Platinum, which could stop time? He always chose such devious moments to pause it.
This time resumed the instant after Lu Mingfei said, “I actually like...”

The next words stuck in his throat. Lu Mingze's voice buzzed in his mind over and over. Every muscle in his body tensed, his face stiffened, as if he were about to launch a missile and discovered it was aimed at the wrong target, and wanted to swallow it back. But it was too late: “I actually like” was already out, Chen Wenwen had heard it... and that damned blush was spreading across her face!
“I actually... liked you,” Lu Mingfei forced out with all his strength.

At last, at last he overcame the rhythm of the sentence and shoved in the past tense. He felt utterly drained. It had been a battle between heaven and man: in that single second, Lu Mingfei had beaten back the little soul wriggling inside him. One step forward was a pretty girl; one step back meant continuing his miserable single life in the autumn wind. The eager little soul shouted, I refuse, I refuse, I refuse... and was suppressed deep in his heart again.

In a setting like this, “I like you” was easy to say. Everything had been arranged for that sentence. He had drunk two glasses of wine, desire stirred in his heart, and a bold declaration would have been perfectly natural; even if Chen Wenwen refused, it wouldn't be too awkward. The wine and feast weren't innocent, and if she dared come alone she should have been prepared like Guan Yunchang attending the enemy's banquet armed with a single blade!
“I used to like you” was difficult. Why bring up something already over when everything was so pleasant? Did he want to put a period at the end of it all?
“I know. You don't have to say it.” The blush faded from Chen Wenwen's face. She lowered her head and spoke softly.
Lu Mingfei coughed violently. That dangerous change of breath had nearly killed him.

He didn't know whether this counted as a victory over Lu Mingze. He didn't like what Lu Mingze said about power. Chen Wenwen was his classmate; he had liked her very much, and even now was willing to stand up for her. However he changed, he would never bend down and pick her up like a tissue. To Lu Mingfei, Chen Wenwen was Chen Wenwen. If she sent him for a Coke now as she once had, he would still jump up and run.
Some things... would never change!
Lu Mingfei gritted his teeth as though defying someone.
“Actually, I knew before too, but I pretended I didn't... I'm sorry I disappointed you,” Chen Wenwen said quietly.

“It's all right, I don't blame you, really. Believe me.” Lu Mingfei took a deep breath, arranging his words with care. “Before I met you, I didn't know what it was like to like a girl. Knowing you taught me. Actually... high school was miserable for me. If I hadn't spent every day mooning over you... it would have been even worse, wouldn't it? I'm grateful you were there. Even though I missed my chance—no, there was never a chance—you can't regret it, can you? If you like someone for that long, they become tied to your past. If you regret having liked them, aren't you denying all the time you lived before?”
He had nothing more to say. He licked his lips and swallowed, embarrassed. “That was too literary. Bear with me.”
“It's all right.” Chen Wenwen lowered her head. “It was beautiful, like poetry.”
“Like poetry?” Lu Mingfei wiped his sweat with a tissue. No one had ever praised him like that before, and he was a little lost.

But there was nothing left to say... Deadlock, absolute deadlock! Everything was on the table now, plain to see. Anything more would be superfluous. It was like the Japanese art of iaido: a sword was alive in its sheath, but once drawn, it was dead.

Should they continue talking about their old classmates? Would Chen Wenwen suddenly stand, burst into tears, and run away? Or would they clasp all four hands and say, ha ha ha, our old misunderstanding is settled, let's drink till we drop tonight? If Chen Wenwen could accept that last possibility... Lu Mingfei would be quite happy to oblige...
The door creaked open. A furtive figure poked his head in and edged inside, peering toward the only lit table, carrying something in his hand.
“What the hell! Brother, are you dropping in for a meal or a room at an inn?” Before a waiter could stop him, Lu Mingfei slapped the table. “Come over here!”

“An... interview.” The man, who had REPORTER written all over his face, clutched a recorder, sweating at the opulent surroundings. He pointed to the camera operator behind him. “This is my younger sister... she does the filming... We're from a TV food show. We heard a gourmet had booked Aspasia tonight and the executive chef was cooking personally, so we came through the rain for an interview. Sorry to disturb you... I'll... I'll leave right away.”
“You came all this way. Why leave? Sit down and eat with us!” Lu Mingfei quickly grabbed his sleeve. Brother, save me! Don't go! If you leave, we'll run out of things to say again.

“Oh, that's too kind. It's awfully expensive.” The reporter was astonished to find the wealthy gourmet so young and hospitable. He rubbed his hands. “I couldn't impose on you for a meal, but could you say a few words to our viewers?”

“No need to stand on ceremony!” Young Master Lu warmly pulled the reporter into a seat, fetched a chair for the camera girl, and called to the waiter. “Chopsticks... no, two more place settings. The menu, the menu! We're ordering more!”
“Well, then... it'd be rude to refuse.” The reporter was delighted. “Brother, how's the food here?”
Lu Mingfei recalled Lu Mingze's expression and smacked his lips. “The tuna is perfectly seared, but if I'd made it, I'd season it with matsutake rather than truffle.”
“And does the wine suit your palate?”
“Of the five great Bordeaux estates, Margaux is my least favorite. It's a Bordeaux vineyard, but its wine tastes a little like Burgundy.” Lu Mingfei pointed at the bottle and frowned.
“And the atmosphere?”

Lu Mingfei nodded slightly, showing his approval. “Mm... the antique ship harmonizes with the aged elm floor, but the designer has divided the space in a very modern way with marble and resin panels. Old and new fit together beautifully; it's private yet open.”
“That's what I said!” The reporter slapped his thigh. “An expert is an expert! We've finally found someone who really knows food.”

Wine was poured, dishes added, and everyone enjoyed themselves. Lu Mingfei and the reporter slapped each other's shoulders and called each other brother. Then he turned and saw Chen Wenwen smiling silently, her expression hard to read: calm, perhaps, or sad.
Brilliant lights flashed across the rain-spattered glass. The dark-blue Panamera stopped beneath a tree outside. Its window lowered and rose again; Chu Zihang nodded expressionlessly to Lu Mingfei.
“Oh, I have to go. Take your time, brother.” Lu Mingfei wiped his mouth with a napkin, stood, and slung his backpack over one shoulder.
“Mm, I'll see you out.” Chen Wenwen stood too.
When the door opened, cold wind rushed in. Rain filled the night, and a handmade black iron lantern cast a warm halo through it.
“You're a really good person,” Chen Wenwen said softly behind him.

Lu Mingfei's heart jumped. He turned and nearly collided with her; she had followed closely, head lowered, as if too tired to do anything but rest it against his back. The warm scent of her hair filled his nose. That restless little soul inside him began muttering again: Idiot, idiot, you've said it now, and there's no chance left.
Lu Mingfei gave a crooked, bitter smile. “Don't hand me the good-guy rejection card whenever you feel like it... We're just classmates having dinner tonight...”
“Thank you. I know you don't like me anymore.” Chen Wenwen shook her head. “But thank you anyway... I don't like you that way either... It's not that I don't like you, just not that kind of liking.”
“Mm-hm.” Lu Mingfei nodded, thoroughly confused.
“When I said you'd changed, I didn't mean money or taste or anything. I meant... well, you've grown up.” She smoothed the hair beside her ear and raised her head, her eyes clear.
“You sound like my big sister...”
“It's wonderful.” Chen Wenwen sighed very, very softly.

“That BMW will take you home.” Lu Mingfei stuck out his tongue. “Don't stand on ceremony with them; it's paid for... To be honest, I'm flat broke in America. Chu Zihang was showing off. He arranged the restaurant, the fancy car, these clothes, all of it. I was fooling the reporter. The food and wine here are good, but they're really not to my taste.”
“I guessed.” Chen Wenwen smiled. “You weren't paying attention to what you ate.”

“Mm... This is the only thing I prepared. It's for you.” He hesitated, then pulled a handful of crumpled plants from his bag and laid them on the table. “Dandelions... I picked them on the way. But at this time of year the little parachutes have all flown away; I couldn't find any whole ones. It doesn't mean anything special, just a keepsake. I wanted to give you dandelions at graduation, so this makes up for it... I remember you picked a lot and put them in a paper bag of bellflowers. When you blew on them, it looked like snow.”
Chen Wenwen looked down, holding the withered bouquet without speaking, and gently stroked its empty stems.
“Goodbye,” she said.
“Goodbye,” Lu Mingfei said.

He pushed open the door and looked up at the rain pouring from the sky. Pulling his collar over his head, he grabbed his suitcase and ran. The Panamera's door swung open and he dove into the passenger seat before looking back. Across the curtain of rain, on the other side of the floor-to-ceiling windows, the air-conditioning scattered the last tiny parachutes. Chen Wenwen stood amid the drifting dandelion seeds, as though she might float away with those soft white things. Looking toward him, she breathed a small patch of mist onto the glass and drew a smiling face in three strokes.
The Panamera raced along the airport expressway. Rain struck the windshield head-on and broke into sprays of water.

“Mission complete.” Steering with one hand, Chu Zihang reached back and patted the sealed aluminum case on the rear seat, then handed Lu Mingfei an iPad. “I've finished the report. Just add your electronic signature at the bottom.”
Too lazy to read it, Lu Mingfei scrawled something in the reporter field and handed the iPad back. “Senior, you never planned to take me on the mission, did you?”
Chu Zihang was silent for a moment. “You're not ready. I don't know why you were appointed commissioner, but you haven't had the necessary training and aren't capable of carrying out an operation.”
Lu Mingfei leaned back, watching the rain pour outside, and sighed. “Hey... I know I'm useless, but you could at least spare my feelings... Just saying I'm not ready like that...”
Some lilting Irish music played on the stereo. Chu Zihang didn't reply, and Lu Mingfei couldn't think of anything to say either. They sat through the silence.
“About tonight... I won't tell Nono,” Chu Zihang said suddenly.

“Thanks.” Lu Mingfei scratched his head. “But senior, get this straight: Nono is Caesar's girlfriend. I'm single, and I'm free to eat with anyone I want. You make it sound like I've done something wrong...”
“But you don't want her to know.” Chu Zihang's answer was as hard and cold as stone.

Lu Mingfei felt he really had nothing to discuss with the president. His way of speaking was like using a knife: the fewest words struck straight at the heart of the matter, hard and accurately, and then the blade was withdrawn. He couldn't be bothered with an extra word.
Chu Zihang was right. Lu Mingfei didn't want Nono to know he'd made a grand show of dining with Chen Wenwen, although he knew Nono wouldn't be angry even if told; at most she'd tease him.
“But Caesar made your reservation. I can't guarantee he won't tell Nono,” Chu Zihang added.

Lu Mingfei nearly choked, just short of rolling his eyes. Hey, boss! You're messing with me, aren't you? Caesar is Nono's boyfriend. What wouldn't he tell her? Please, use some sense! All right, you've been single so long you probably don't know what boyfriends and girlfriends are like...

“The restaurant had a wedding banquet tonight and wasn't taking individual guests, but I'd already told Chen Wenwen and couldn't easily change it. It was no problem for Caesar. He's a Mint Club member, and that club can do almost anything.”
“Caesar helped you?” Lu Mingfei was curious.

“I posted a reward on the Night Watcher forum. Anyone who could reserve a table for you would be owed a favor by me.” Chu Zihang's voice was as level as the asphalt beneath the wheels. “Caesar would see it too, of course. He's the noble young master of the Gattuso family and wouldn't let anyone court his subordinates from a position above him. So he'd rush to take care of it first. Caesar is very possessive, not only of his subordinates but also of his enemies. He wouldn't let anyone else claim my reward and interfere in our competition. He considers me his enemy, so he wants to defeat me himself.”
“So you tricked Boss? Senior, you're devious!”
“People who speak little are often devious.” Chu Zihang's tone was mild. “Actually, I'm sure Caesar understood exactly what I was thinking, but he was willing to play along.”

Lu Mingfei grinned. Worrying was useless now; he'd just have to wait for Nono to find out and tease him. Even if Chu Zihang had played him, he had been irresolute himself, unable to move when he saw Chen Wenwen. Then again, he had no reason to be resolute in the first place.
“Senior, you really have influence. Chen Wenwen actually agreed to dinner.”
“I used your name, gave her the restaurant's card, and asked whether she would refuse. She said yes. That was it.” Chu Zihang said, “I'm not good at invitations.”
“Is that how you've always invited girls to dinner?” Lu Mingfei was speechless. “Like you're challenging them on their own turf.”
Chu Zihang nodded.
“That works?”
Chu Zihang thought about it. “I don't remember anyone refusing.”
Lu Mingfei sighed. “All right, you win... You don't know how ridiculous tonight was. A reporter from a food show came to interview me, and I fed him a whole load of nonsense.”

“I called their show and said someone had booked Aspasia tonight for a dinner for two, with the executive chef cooking personally. They were curious and said they'd send a reporter. When the interview airs, Zhao Menghua will see it too. A man like him probably thinks, ‘Even if I don't want it, no one else may touch it.’ Imagine his face when he sees the show. Wouldn't that be fun?” Chu Zihang said.
Lu Mingfei glanced at him in surprise. With that cold, hard face, he didn't even smile while saying something so quietly malicious; there wasn't the slightest hint he thought it fun.
“Vicious! I'm impressed!” Lu Mingfei said.
The Panamera abruptly slowed. Chu Zihang wrenched the wheel and braked sharply at the side of the airport expressway.

“Hey, hey! I was only talking nonsense! It's raining outside, senior! I'll catch cold if you make me stand in it!” Lu Mingfei hurriedly said. Last time he'd been inexplicably kicked out of the car to bake in the sun for several minutes.
Chu Zihang waved a hand. “Wait in the car for me.”
Lu Mingfei stared, his gaze falling on Chu Zihang's waist. “Holy crap... Senior, you're bleeding!”

A striking red stain spread across Chu Zihang's white shirt. Only now did Lu Mingfei notice that his face was pale as if dusted with powder—not because he was posing, but because he'd lost so much blood.
“It's nothing. The wound reopened,” Chu Zihang said lightly.

He opened the door and got out into the pouring rain. He unbuttoned his shirt and tossed it into the car, then unwound the layers of gauze from his waist. Bare-chested, head lowered, he stood in the downpour and let it wash over him. His abdomen was streaked with blood, and the wound looked alarming.

“Huh? What's the point of a shirtless wet-body show now? We're on the expressway!” Lu Mingfei was shocked. “If you really want to look cool and outrageous... Senior, you could take your pants off too...”

But he soon understood. As the rain washed away the blood, faint white steam rose, like concentrated sulfuric acid mixed with water, or as if Chu Zihang's blood were burning oil. Water mixed with blood splashed onto the ground, leaving white spots. Lu Mingfei stared, reminded of the monster in Alien whose blood was strong acid. He had just been chatting with such a monster and riding in his car; he didn't know whether to be proud or scream.
Only when the blood had washed away did Chu Zihang return to the car. He dried himself quickly and took fresh clothes from his suitcase.
“Don't tell anyone. Consider it repayment for my favor,” he said quietly.
“No problem, no problem!” Lu Mingfei nodded vigorously.
“Thank you.” Chu Zihang started the Panamera. “May I ask a question? Do you like Nono more, or Chen Wenwen?”
“Senior, could you not be so nosy when you're asking someone to keep a secret?” Lu Mingfei made a miserable face.
“Oh, sorry,” Chu Zihang said mildly.

The Panamera returned to the road. “I once read a book called Shanghai Fortress. It said there are twenty thousand people in the world you'll fall in love with at first sight, but you might never meet a single one in your whole life,” Lu Mingfei said suddenly.
Chu Zihang blinked. “I didn't expect there to be so many...”

“I really liked Chen Wenwen in high school. If she'd liked me back, I probably wouldn't have come to Cassell to slay dragons, and I wouldn't have met Nono. Shameless as it sounds, I like Nono now, but I think I'm just mooning over her, like I did with Chen Wenwen.” Lu Mingfei hung his head. “Who I like doesn't matter, does it? The question is who will like me.”
“You're the only S-rank among us. You shouldn't think like that,” Chu Zihang said.
“You all make S-rank sound impressive, but I can't feel it. You don't even bother taking me on operations,” Lu Mingfei muttered.

“That's because you don't have enough experience yet. This world is ours, and yours too, but one day it will all be yours,” Chu Zihang said softly. “That day you'll take the places of Caesar and me on the battlefield.”

Lu Mingfei immediately imagined himself taking Chu Zihang's place before the three-nothings girl. She waved a hand and rolling flames swept over the three realms like a blazing red lotus, a furious tide of light surging toward him. He, an S-rank, waved a hand too... nothing. He could only say, “Hello, have you eaten?” Then the fire passed, leaving him standing in the ruins as a blackened human shape with only two pitiful eyes blinking... Though it was rather cute, when he pictured it.
“Senior, do you really think my bloodline is S-rank?”
“I don't know. You haven't shown a bloodline advantage yet.” Chu Zihang was blunt.

Lu Mingfei sighed. “It's not that I don't want to be impressive. I used to show off in my fantasies. I'd daydream in class about how cool I'd be one day: the teacher is explaining English grammar when a beautiful girl comes in and says in perfect American English, ‘Sorry to interrupt, but Sir Lu Mingfei, an urgent transoceanic call from headquarters. If you don't answer, North America will sink...’ Then, in front of the whole class, I take the phone and rattle away in flawless French. From then on the teacher never dares punish me by making me copy vocabulary.” He smiled self-mockingly. “But that wouldn't be me at all. It'd be somebody else with nothing to do with me.”
Chu Zihang glanced at him. “What kind of person do you think you are?”

“Probably... the kind who sleeps in, plays games, spaces out and thinks about random things, reads magazines for free at the newsstand, and likes someone for three years without daring to confess... I know that kind of person isn't interesting. But that's who I am.” Lu Mingfei hesitated. “Senior, do you know? When I first walked into Aspasia, I was bursting with happiness, imagining what I'd say if Chen Wenwen liked me because I rescued her and treated her to such an expensive meal, thinking I was incredibly cool.”
“She watched you through the glass the whole time you left. I saw it in the rearview mirror,” Chu Zihang said. “She did like you a little, didn't she? But you ran away.”

“Yeah.” Lu Mingfei nodded seriously. “Because then it wouldn't be me she liked. I didn't even know what Aspasia was. I don't have Boss's taste, much less a Mint Club membership. I can't afford to treat her to a meal that expensive; my credit card is still in debt. Boss was really the one buying her Italian food. Boss is wonderful, of course; any girl would like him, right? If I treated her, I could only afford ramen at a street stall... But the me who can only afford ramen still hopes someone will like him...” He scratched his head, suddenly embarrassed. “I'm making a mess of this... Senior, do you understand?”

The corner of Chu Zihang's eye twitched almost imperceptibly, and he fell silent. After a long time he reached out and patted Lu Mingfei's shoulder. “I understand... There used to be someone who could only drive a car, and hoped people would like the him who could only drive.”
Lu Mingfei sensed his senior was showing him a little closeness, but didn't understand the deeper meaning, so he could only grin in response.

“What a person can accomplish doesn't depend entirely on bloodline, but on what he wants to accomplish. When I say you're not ready, I don't mean your blood or your ability. I mean you have no goal,” Chu Zihang said. “There's no goal that would make you put everything on the line and use all your strength. Someone who can't do that is useless, even if his bloodline is stronger than all of ours.”

“Who would I put everything on the line for...” Lu Mingfei muttered. He remembered seeing the sharp tail spike pierce Nono's chest underwater at the Three Gorges, her hair floating like thick seaweed in a cloud of her own blood. His fingers had grown hot and he'd wanted desperately to draw that blade. The feeling had been wonderful. He too wanted another chance to throw everything away for someone in a flash of passion... but what right did he have to risk himself for anyone?
“Everyone has reasons to risk their life. You keep your life... to wait for the day you'll put it on the line,” Chu Zihang said softly.

Only after speaking did he realize how sentimental it sounded. He and Lu Mingfei weren't close enough to bare their hearts; they were merely partners on one operation. He said no more, pressed the accelerator hard, and the engine revved. The Panamera became a dark-blue streak of lightning on the expressway.

The night sky was deep blue, and the glacier below it was black. It was nearly midnight. The moon had just risen over the glacier, turning ice accumulated over tens of thousands of years a luminous blue. Wolves howled from some unknown direction, startling sleeping birds into flight from the dark forest. The Hailuogou hot-spring resort lay in a hollow beneath the glacier.

Nono and Susie soaked in a square hot-spring pool. Under the lights, the water was a soft baby blue, fine wisps of steam rising from its surface. Nono lifted a long leg from the water, waving a razor in her hand.
“Please, you hardly have any leg hair.” Susie took a cold can of Coke from a little wooden boat floating in front of her.
“I'm imitating Marilyn Monroe's pose.” Nono ducked under the water and popped up beside Susie like a little fish. “Tell me, what's sexy about shaving your legs?”
“I'm not a man. Ask Caesar.” Susie sounded languid.

“Caesar thinks a troupe of girls in white lace dresses is the sexiest thing. He's already recruited a whole group into the Student Council.” Nono narrowed her eyes and smiled. “Do you think Chu Zihang would like it? Maybe I should make a show of shaving for him one day?”

“You should do it for Lu Mingfei. The recoil from his nosebleed would send him to the moon.” Susie pinched her friend's nose. “You remember, don't you? It's Lu Mingfei's birthday. He's your only little junior. Did you text him?”
“I remember, I remember, but I'm hesitating a little.” Nono put a white towel soaked in cold water on her forehead and looked up at the sky.
“Don't tell me you don't know he likes you?”
“Do I look that stupid?” Nono made a face. “I've been dating since kindergarten!”
“Kindergarten?”

“I'm the queen of all big sisters. I once stood at the front of my kindergarten class and pointed at all the little boys, announcing that from that day on they were all my boyfriends and had to obey me, and anyone who didn't would be kicked out!” Nono smiled, showing her lovely teeth, her sterling-silver four-leaf clover earrings swaying.
“What's it like, having a junior secretly in love with you?”
“Like an older man in kindergarten telling you what a pretty little girl you are.”
“What do you mean?”

“The man says you're pretty, and the junior likes you, but neither of them really knows you. Next time the man sees another little girl he'll tell her she's pretty too, and the junior will end up with a younger girl.” Nono shrugged and climbed onto a step beside the pool. Though she wore a swimsuit, much of her chest was exposed, and when the water ran off, a recently healed scar was visible. She had received it during the Three Gorges Reservoir operation, but no longer remembered what had caused it. The doctor had marveled that whatever huge, deadly weapon had made it, her survival was a miracle.
“Plenty of people have crushes on you, don't they? Does Caesar know? Isn't he worried?”

“Caesar is actually very perceptive. He can sense who likes me.” Nono tilted her head, combing through her dark-red hair. “But he isn't worried, much less jealous. He thinks only he deserves me. Of course, if the one who liked me were Chu Zihang...” Nono's eyes curved like crescent moons. “Then Caesar might get serious about dealing with him. Thinking about it makes me want to seduce your Chu Zihang!”
“Chu Zihang can't be seduced. Even if you ran toward him naked through the snow, he'd think you had a fever and needed cooling down,” Susie said mildly.
“Hey, I'm joking. Don't be possessive. I won't touch your Chu Zihang.” Nono cautiously nudged Susie's shoulder.

“He isn't mine. You don't think he's my boyfriend too, do you? He's just a good friend. He's willing to do things for me only because he thinks I've helped him. That's how he is: anyone who helps him, he makes sure to repay. You helped him with your profiling today; maybe he'll take you to dinner when school starts.” Susie smiled.
Nono sighed and patted her head. “That makes me angry enough to cry. What a jerk. When I get back to college, I'll teach him a lesson for you.”

“He just doesn't have many feelings.” Susie fell silent for a while, then, not wanting to continue the subject, turned and tapped Nono's nose. “Seriously, you've been dating Caesar almost two years. Are you going to marry him?”

Nono rested her chin on her hand and thought for a long time, then shook her head. “I haven't decided... I mean it. It's not that there's anything wrong with Caesar. He's very, very good to me, but I don't know why I should marry him!”
“I asked my mom that,” Susie said. “Her answer was... because only after you're married can you register the children in the household records!”
Nono covered her face. “Your mom is amazing!”
“Maybe you don't need a reason. Keep it simple: you like someone, he's good to you, you want to stay with him forever, so you marry him and make him yours,” Susie said.
“You like Chu Zihang. How long will you like him?” Nono asked softly, gazing at the night sky.

Susie looked up. Moonlight reflected in Nono's clear pupils, and her face was uncharacteristically blank. Knowing she had something on her mind, Susie grew serious too. “I don't know. Maybe once I find a boyfriend, I won't like him anymore.”
“If Chu Zihang suddenly proposed and you married him, you wouldn't have another boyfriend. Would you go on liking him all your life?”
Susie thought for a while and shook her head. “I don't know. I've never liked anyone for a lifetime.”
“You don't really know Chu Zihang, do you? Even though you remember perfectly whether he likes his eggs fried on one side or both.”
Susie lowered her head. “He hasn't given me a chance to know him.”

“Exactly.” Nono looked down into Susie's eyes, very serious. “When you first begin to like someone, that's when you know them least. Take Chu Zihang: a handsome, cool guy with an expressionless face, but you have no idea when he's happy or sad. He's a book whose cover hasn't even opened for you. Yet you keep thinking about him, longing to open that book and read what's inside. Maybe one day you'll be together and you'll open it. It's so wonderful that you forget to eat and sleep, and want to take it even to the bathroom... But after one year, two years, five, ten, you've finished it and memorized every line and word. Will you still read it over and over? Or will you put it back in its cover and set it on a shelf? Books on shelves are rarely opened again.”

Susie was silent for a long time, then reached out and touched Nono's cheek affectionately. “Doesn't it tire you, having so much on your mind all day? Caesar is already the ultimate boyfriend. What kind of person do you want to marry?”

“I've thought about it!” Nono's eyes shone. “The man I marry will make me believe he'll always be with me. As long as I want him there, he'll stay with me always and always. When I'm afraid, even if I can't find anyone else, I'll always find him. When I'm trapped in a nightmare, his name will be the one I call without thinking.”
“Mm.” Susie looked solemn. “In that case, a dog would do... You could name it ‘Oh, how scary,’ and when you have a nightmare you'd call, ‘Oh, how scary!’”
“How dare you tease me, little lady?” Nono plunged into the spring and pushed Susie in too.

Steam hung thick as a curtain. The girls' laughter answered the distant howls of wolves. Nearby, a man selling cold beer, wrapped in an old sheepskin coat, glimpsed lovely curves flashing through the vapor and silently suffered a nosebleed.
Beep, beep. Nono's phone, sealed in a waterproof plastic bag, lit up with a text.
She emerged from the spring, shook the water from her hair, and opened it.
“Dear: This may seem sudden to you, but I've planned it for a long time. Please read this message patiently to the end...”
It was from Caesar Gattuso. Nono's eyes widened in surprise, and she exchanged a glance with Susie, who had leaned over to look.
Portofino, Italy. The Splendid Hotel.

Caesar leaned against a marble column, holding a glass of gin on ice. A single lamp above cast its light straight down around him. Night had fallen and a storm swept across the Gulf of Genoa. The hotel had brought its umbrellas and outdoor café seating inside, leaving him alone in the courtyard. Lights blazed behind him, an indoor band playing gentle blues, while wind and rain darkened the world ahead. From where he stood the pale-gray sea rolled as though an enormous sea beast were about to break the surface. Waves several meters high battered the cliffs below, while a distant lighthouse beam swept monotonously over the water.
Caesar made a call. “Caesar Gattuso. I'd like to know whether my account has been frozen.”

His private banking adviser sounded alarmed. “How could that happen, Mr. Gattuso? You've always been among our highest-tier clients. Who would dare freeze your account? I just checked again and confirmed everything is perfectly normal...”

Caesar silently hung up, unwilling to listen further. Of course there were people in the world who dared freeze his account. His enormous spending came from family funds, and his father or uncle could suspend or permanently close it. He had defied his uncle so fiercely today, and the old man's face had been full of anger when he left, yet he still hadn't thought to freeze Caesar's account. For years Caesar had tested his uncle's limits, and however furious Frost Gattuso became, he had never punished his nephew. Seen from that angle alone, the family's love for Caesar was as vast as the Gulf of Genoa.

Caesar smiled silently. In truth, while spending the family's money freely, he was always prepared for the account to be closed. He knew the conflict between him and the family could not be reconciled. Ever since he'd announced he was considering changing his surname to “Gullveig,” all his elders had flown into a rage. “How could you have such an absurd idea?” “That's a lowly surname!” “You may rebel against anything, but not your blood!” Caesar had looked at those angry old faces and found it fascinating.

If one day he lost that endlessly replenished account, he would say goodbye to his present life: luxury sports cars, top hotels, high society in its perfumes and fine clothes, even the light and warmth behind him. He would walk into the storm alone.
“I can't say I don't care at all.” He stretched out his hand and let the rain fall into his palm.
There was still no reply. He dried his hand and reread the message he had just sent.

“...I once imagined that on the day I proposed, I would pretend to invite you on vacation to an uninhabited island. I'd have my friends wait on the beach across the water with thousands of fireworks. When you and I walked hand in hand to the shore, I would suddenly kneel and bring out the ring I'd prepared, while streaks of light flew across the night sky and reflected in the sea. But when the day suddenly came, I hadn't had time to arrange fireworks. I could buy a ring at once, but I couldn't get it to China. The Mint Club people say the earliest they can deliver it to you is tomorrow morning. But I don't want to wait. I want to say it tonight: Nono, I want to announce our engagement to everyone, in a grand ceremony or a simple one...”
“Wow! Speak of the wolf and it really comes! A proposal text! My face is burning!” Susie covered her cheeks and cried out.
“Hey... he isn't proposing to you...” Nono glanced at her. “Keep reading. I don't know why he's suddenly gone crazy tonight.”
“A man who suddenly goes crazy is the most romantic kind! He must be an absolute Cancer!”
“No, he's a perfectionist Libra!”
Caesar tipped the last of his drink and its ice into his mouth.

“...But it's very likely our engagement won't have my family's blessing. The Gattuso family's chosen heir has his engagement decided by the family, not by himself. But I won't let them decide my future. My future will be brilliant, and I will share it with the brilliant girl I love. Her surname isn't special; her hair is dark red; she wears silver four-leaf-clover earrings; when she's angry she's as prickly and unapproachable as a hedgehog... But I want to live with her for decades more, perhaps a hundred years. I truly have to thank my bloodline: it gives me more time in the life I have left to spend with her...”
Reading that far, Caesar smiled silently. He was beginning to admire his own literary talent. All that idle practice writing fiction online hadn't gone to waste.

“...It's such a lonely night. It's raining in Portofino, and Portofino is beautiful in the rain. I've always wanted to bring you here, but you haven't accepted my invitation yet. Much happened today; I'll tell you everything later. Right now I only want to say that tonight, more than ever, I wish you were beside me. Even if you merely sat silently watching me, or pulled a contemptuous face and mocked my weakness at this moment, I would still want to feel your warmth...”
He set his glass beneath the grapevines and walked into the rain, which instantly soaked him through. He mounted the little motorcycle and rode out through the heavy black iron gates.
“Wow, underneath it all he's a sensitive, proud little boy!” Susie shook a clenched fist. “‘I'm happy even when you bully me’ and all that!”
“Absolutely not.” Nono stuck out her tongue, a blush rising to her cheeks. “Something probably upset him today. Most of the time he's still an overbearing, conceited guy.”
“You're blushing, you're blushing!” Susie leaned over Nono's smooth back and pinched her cheeks.
“Hey, it's a love letter. Isn't it normal to blush reading one?” Nono reached back and pinched her nose. “If you're peeking at somebody else's love letter, be quiet!”
“All right, all right, I'll shut up. Look how ridiculously happy you are.” Susie put her arms around her neck.

“...I have many, many friends, and know many, many girls. Ever since I was little I've wondered what kind of girl I would spend my life with. What a terrifying thing: only one chance to choose, and I must swear before everyone to love and protect her and never leave her. I thought I was already brave, but not brave enough to tell a girl in public that I would love her for life. Then I met you, and you gave me that courage. Yes, Nono, I love you, and I hope for the chance to love you all my life...”
The little motorcycle cut through the storm. Caesar's wet blond hair streamed into the wind like a battle flag, and Anthony the gyrfalcon flew beside him.

“...I know many people think I'm a spoiled playboy or a young emperor or something, but whether he's a playboy or a young emperor, when a man faces the girl he loves, he's only a boy. The boy who loves you is named Caesar, not Caesar Gattuso, just Caesar. There are things I can't tell you yet, but my family doesn't want you and me to become engaged. If I have to choose, however, I will take off the glittering coat called ‘Gattuso’ without hesitation. Would you accept that Caesar? Still Caesar, only apparently naked...”

The motorcycle stopped on the beach. Caesar ran into the cold surf, his powerful chest breaking wave after wave of the rising tide. He threw off his little white dinner jacket, kicked away his expensive crocodile-skin shoes, tied his hair back with the violet scarf, and dove into the water, swimming against the waves toward the deep sea.

“...Come, we will seize happiness and glory together. My life will be a great ship, and I want you standing with me at its prow. When that ship enters port we will astonish the world together. I will take your hand as we come ashore and say, ‘This is Caesar's bride!’”

His arms stroked powerfully, fighting the cold waves again and again. Caesar felt like an arrow gliding through the water. Nothing could stop him: waves, family, even his father! Because he was sharp enough!

Caesar burst out of the water and looked back. He could no longer see the cliffs through the storm; he was nearing the edge of the harbor. Around him were only black, heaving waves. The lighthouse's white beam swept past, and a falcon's cry tore through the wind and rain.
“Anthony! Fly! Fly to...” Caesar raised his arm and shouted at the sky with all his strength. “The highest place!”
In the black sky torn by lightning, the falcon soared.
Thousands of kilometers away, at Hailuogou in China's Sichuan Province, snowflakes settled on the girls' bare arms and quickly melted into drops of water.

“It's snowing.” Susie sank into the hot spring, watching the fine drifting flakes. “So beautiful. I never expected snow this time of year. It must be a blessing for you, though the proposal reads a little like a declaration of war...”
“Come conquer the world with me, woman!” Nono sank into the spring too, curling up with her mouth beneath the surface, only her blinking eyes showing, like a child.

“But it's really moving, as though he put all his strength into every word,” Susie said softly. “If Lu Mingfei wrote it, it'd probably be something like, ‘I don't mean anything special, I just thought if we have children it'll be easier to register them,’ that sort of nonsense.”
“Hey... where did that strange idea come from?” Nono said quietly.
